papers.title: Neuron-OPSD: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
papers.authors: Zhuowei Chen, Xiang Lorraine Li et al.
papers.abstract_summary: Proposes Neuron On-Policy Self-Distillation (Neuron-OPSD), a data-centric framework for annotation-free self-distillation that leverages internal neuron activations to guide both training-data selection and teacher context construction. Trained via on-policy distillation from the teacher distribution, requiring no ground-truth labels. Improves in-domain task performance while preserving cross-domain generalization and mitigating calibration collapse.
papers.incremental_note: Published July 2, 2026. Extends neuron-aware selection to annotation-free settings. Complements NAIT (baseline) which uses neuron activations for instruction data selection.

papers.title: HERMES: A Multi-Granularity Labeling Substrate for Pre-training Data Mixtures
papers.authors: Ziyun Qiao, Yue Min, Ruining Chen et al.
papers.abstract_summary: Proposes a hierarchical data-derived labeling substrate using Learned Semantic Transform + 3-stage residual vector quantization that annotates each document into a coarse-to-fine code (~130k cells). Argues the bottleneck in data mixing is the label system, not the mixer. At one prefix length, combined Stage-2 rule lifts 16-task capability macro-average by +0.0253. Reframes data mixture design from choosing fixed label sets to navigating a reusable granularity hierarchy.
papers.incremental_note: Published July 2, 2026. Novel perspective: the label system (not the mixer) is the bottleneck for data mixing. Enables hierarchical granularity control.

papers.title: Holistic Data Scheduler (HDS): Online Data Mixing via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Chenhao Dang, Jing Ma, Mingjie Liao et al.
papers.abstract_summary: Formulates data scheduling as a reinforcement learning problem using Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm. Introduces multi-objective holistic reward integrating data-driven (quality), loss-driven (inter-domain influence), and model-driven (weight norms) perspectives. Reaches final validation perplexity of next best method with 44% fewer training iterations on The Pile. Achieves 7.2% improvement on MMLU 0-shot. KDD 2026.
papers.incremental_note: KDD 2026 (pp. 176-187). Novel RL formulation for online data mixing with 44% training efficiency gain. Code released on GitHub.

papers.title: TiKMiX: Efficient Semi-Dynamic Data Mixture via Data Influence for LLM Pre-training
papers.authors: Yifan Wang, Binbin Liu, Fengze Liu, Yuanfan Guo, Jiyao Deng, Xuecheng Wu, Weidong Zhou, Xiaohuan Zhou, Taifeng Wang
papers.abstract_summary: Proposes semi-dynamic data mixing grounded in influence ranking invariance: relative importance of data domains exhibits strong temporal stability over long training intervals. Introduces Group Influence for efficient domain impact quantification. Compared with RegMix, reduces computational overhead by 80% and achieves average 2% performance gain across nine downstream benchmarks. ACL 2026 Long Paper.
papers.incremental_note: ACL 2026 Long Paper (pp. 5777-5793). 80% compute reduction vs RegMix. Key insight: domain influence rankings are temporally stable.

papers.title: LLMSurgeon: Diagnosing Data Mixture of Large Language Models
papers.authors: Yaxin Luo, Jiacheng Cui, Xiaohan Zhao, Xinyi Shang, Jiacheng Liu, Xinyue Bi, Zhaoyi Li, Zhiqiang Shen
papers.abstract_summary: Formalizes Data Mixture Surgery (DMS): given only generated text from a target LLM, estimate the domain-level distribution of its pretraining corpus. Casts DMS as inverse problem under label-shift assumption, estimates calibrated soft confusion matrix to recover latent mixture prior. Introduces LLMScan evaluation suite built from open-source LLMs with transparent pretraining mixtures. Code: github.com/Yaxin9Luo/LLMSurgeon. ACL 2026 Long Paper.
papers.incremental_note: ACL 2026 Long Paper (pp. 42444-42459). Novel post-hoc auditing tool for data mixture provenance. Code released.

papers.title: DataEvolver: Automatic Data Preparation for Large Language Models through Multi-Level Self-Evolving
papers.authors: Chao Deng, Shaolei Zhang, Ju Fan et al.
papers.abstract_summary: First self-evolving data preparation system that automatically constructs pipelines to transform raw data into high-quality data. Multi-level mechanism: operator level incrementally expands operator set; pipeline level iteratively refines orchestration via feedback loop reducing distribution gap. Achieves average 10% gain in downstream LLM performance across seven benchmarks compared to training on original data.
papers.incremental_note: June 2026. First system to auto-evolve entire data preparation pipeline. 10% average LLM performance gain from automated curation.

papers.title: Explaining Data Mixing Scaling Laws
papers.abstract_summary: Proposes unified framework to explain mechanics of data mixing by extending Kaplan/Chinchilla scaling laws to multi-domain setting. Identifies two key factors: Capacity Competition (finite capacity couples domain losses globally) and Noise Reduction (optimal weights shift toward harder-to-learn domains). Successfully extrapolates across scales using significantly fewer parameters than empirical laws. ICML 2026. Code: github.com/meiqwq/Explaining-Data-Mixing-Scaling-Laws.
papers.incremental_note: ICML 2026. First theoretical explanation of data mixing scaling laws. Enables cross-scale mixture prediction with fewer parameters.

papers.title: Data filtering methods for training language models
papers.authors: Egor Shevchenko, Elena Bruches et al.
papers.abstract_summary: Comparative analysis of Confident Learning and Dataset Cartography for label error detection on three Russian text classification corpora. Results show effectiveness depends on dataset characteristics: large corpora with low noise see no improvement from filtering, while small noisy datasets benefit significantly from Confident Learning. AINL-2026.
papers.incremental_note: AINL-2026. Narrow scope (Russian NLP) but provides practical guidance on when filtering helps vs. when it doesn't.

papers.title: Difficulty-Diversity Collaborative Filtering (DDCF) for Data-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract_summary: Proposes Difficulty-Diversity Collaborative Filtering (DDCF) that automatically selects a core set for fine-tuning by balancing difficulty and diversity. Reduces both annotating and fine-tuning costs. Uses lambda=0.2 to balance core set quality without eroding pre-trained knowledge.
papers.incremental_note: 2026. Novel difficulty-diversity trade-off framework for fine-tuning data selection.

papers.title: Data mixing can induce phase transitions in knowledge acquisition
papers.abstract_summary: Formalizes how data mixing ratio or dataset size variations can induce phase transitions in LLM knowledge acquisition. Models a sufficiently trained LLM as learning from mixture of knowledge-dense and knowledge-sparse domains, identifying critical thresholds where mixing ratio changes qualitatively alter knowledge acquisition patterns.
key_methods: phase transition theory for data mixing
papers.incremental_note: NeurIPS 2025. Theoretical perspective on data mixing: phase transitions in knowledge acquisition. Missed by baseline and prior incrementals.
